subject.title: add option for MCP apps support

question: After the two mechanical defects and exact-head proof are resolved, should OpenClaw accept the default-off trust model where configured MCP servers may supply sandboxed executable UI and invoke app-visible methods on their owning server?
rationale: Code review can assess isolation mechanics, but accepting executable third-party UI plus delegated MCP calls in core Control UI is a product and security policy choice; the protected maintainer label also requires explicit human handling.

options.title: Accept the opt-in boundary
options.body: Keep `mcp.apps.enabled` default-off and land after exact-head proof and focused fixes confirm the documented isolation and server-scoping guarantees.

options.title: Narrow the initial release
options.body: Ship isolated rendering first and defer app-initiated tool and resource bridge calls until a later security review.

options.title: Do not host Apps in core
options.body: Close or redesign the feature if executable MCP-provided UI is outside the intended Control UI trust model.

recommendation.title: Accept the opt-in boundary
recommendation.body: Keep `mcp.apps.enabled` default-off and land after exact-head proof and focused fixes confirm the documented isolation and server-scoping guarantees.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the current hardened implementation and explicitly authorized its official bridge dependency on the exact head.
